analysis: Examined four changed files. (1) docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: documentation-only edits to the GLM native prompt contract table (lines 1147-1155) plus a date bump. Reasoning null and summary no-ops are accepted. Thinking-off, include_reasoning:false and exclusion are explicit refusals. JSON response_format and tool_choice forced modes are described as post-validated, with output withheld until validation passes and a 422 with no content on non-compliance. These claims are fail-closed and do not add a trust grant or a wire field. They state that unqualified modes (media, constrained decoding) are not qualified, so they do not overclaim per T-056. The code behind the claims (GLM5NextPromptPolicy, ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy, NativeToolStreamRouter) is not in the supplied evidence, so the behavior is unverified. (2) fixtures/prompt-contract/glm53-flash/README.md: wording change only. It now says strict tools, forced choice and JSON are served via output validation and that the fixtures do not qualify them. (3) NativeServeQualification.swift line 32-33: adds DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, pointing at the private 0700 state directory, to the diagnostic env map. This confines the verified-weights record to the qualification directory and keeps it off the operator's real state. That is a mild hardening and has no regression. The consumer of the env var is outside the evidence. (4) libs/mlx-swift-lm: submodule pointer bump from 7bed821 to baca4ac. The content of the diff is not supplied, so the inference-engine dependency change (TB-007, A-001, T-028, T-041) cannot be reviewed. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Recommend reviewing the submodule diff, particularly KV cache, memory and prompt handling, and the GLM-related provider-swift source changes if they exist in other batches.
